$comment: Google Play facts the checkers compare against, each with its source. Verified 2026-10-14. Re-verify: open each source; for the SDK levels read node_modules/react-native/gradle/libs.versions.toml; for BundleConfig read github.com/google/bundletool src/main/proto/config.proto. Change a value only with its new source and date.
targetSdkSource: developer.android.com/google/play/requirements/target-sdk: from 2026-08-31 new apps and app updates must target Android 16 (API level 36) or higher (Wear OS and Automotive 35, TV and XR 34); extension forms to 2026-11-01. React Native 0.86.3 (Expo SDK 57) targets 36 by default.
versionCodeSource: developer.android.com/studio/publish/versioning: the greatest versionCode Google Play allows is 2100000000; a versionCode Play has seen can never be uploaded again.
pageSizeSource: developer.android.com/guide/practices/page-sizes: apps targeting Android 15 (API 35) and higher must support 16 KB pages on 64-bit devices; from 2027-02-01 updates that do not are refused. Every PT_LOAD segment aligned to 2**14 or more; bundletool dump config shows PAGE_ALIGNMENT_16K.
abiSource: developer.android.com/google/play/requirements/64-bit: every app with 32-bit native code ships the 64-bit version of it too.

declarationPermissions.$comment: Permissions Play reviews against a declaration in Play Console (Policy and programs, App content, or the Permissions declaration form). A bundle that holds one needs the contract entry's playDeclaration naming what was declared. Verified sources: support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/10158779 (QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES) and answer/14115180 (photo and video); the other entries follow the Play Console Help topics of the same names (SMS and call log, location in the background, foreground service types, advertising ID, exact alarms, full-screen intents, accessibility, VpnService) and are marked unverified-by-fetch here: re-check the current list in Play Console before a release that adds a permission.
declarationPermissions.android.permission.QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES: Permissions declaration form: broad package visibility
declarationPermissions.android.permission.MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORA: Permissions declaration form: all files access
declarationPermissions.android.permission.REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKA: Permissions declaration form: request install packages
declarationPermissions.android.permission.READ_MEDIA_IMAGES: Photo and video permissions declaration (prefer the system photo picker)
declarationPermissions.android.permission.READ_MEDIA_VIDEO: Photo and video permissions declaration (prefer the system photo picker)
declarationPermissions.android.permission.ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOC: Location permissions declaration with a video of the feature
declarationPermissions.android.permission.READ_SMS: SMS and call log permissions declaration
declarationPermissions.android.permission.RECEIVE_SMS: SMS and call log permissions declaration
declarationPermissions.android.permission.SEND_SMS: SMS and call log permissions declaration
declarationPermissions.android.permission.READ_CALL_LOG: SMS and call log permissions declaration
declarationPermissions.android.permission.WRITE_CALL_LOG: SMS and call log permissions declaration
declarationPermissions.android.permission.PROCESS_OUTGOING_CALL: SMS and call log permissions declaration
declarationPermissions.android.permission.USE_EXACT_ALARM: Exact alarm declaration (alarm and calendar apps only)
declarationPermissions.android.permission.USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTEN: Full-screen intent declaration (calling and alarm apps)

releaseOnlyBlocked.$comment: Permissions the React Native template keeps in the main manifest although only development needs them; a release blocks them with android.blockedPermissions unless the app really uses the feature (then the contract entry says why).
releaseOnlyBlocked.android.permission.SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW: the React Native dev overlay draws over other apps in development builds only
